sources.text: For 25 years, XBOX has remained focused on building games players love, and our anniversary year has been a particularly strong example. From Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , to hugely anticipated games like Fable , players have more great games to play on XBOX than ever. Today, The Game Awards has announced this year’s list of nominees and titles across XBOX’s creative teams have earned eight nominations across multiple categories. Outside of gaming, Prime Video’s ‘Fallout’ has been nominated for Best Adaptation. Thank you to all of the teams that brought these great games to players. Voting is now open on The Game Awards’ official site – tune into The Game Awards on December 10 to see if your favorite games from 2026 take home an award. Our publishing partners also received nominations across a range of categories, with many games available to play today with Game Pass. 007 First Light and CONTROL Resonant are both nominated for Game of the Year and playable across devices with XBOX Play Anywhere. Game Pass subscribers can play nominees like Gears of War: E-Day , Forza Horizon 6 , No Man’s Sky , and more. See below for the full list of nominees playable on XBOX, including Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , and remember you can vote for your favorites right now over at TheGameAwards.com . In the meantime, many of these titles will be available at their lowest prices yet with XBOX’s Black Friday sale, starting November 19 – find out more here . Congratulations to this year’s incredible nominees!

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 | Critical Consensus
sources.text: Critics praise the "richly drawn and compelling romance" of Jason and Lucia in GTA 6, delivering a record Metacritic score After a 13-year wait, Grand Theft Auto 6 has been met with universal acclaim. Despite a lead-up marred by delays and leaks the hype has only grown, with over 17 million pre-orders generating more than $1.6 billion in revenue, according to recent data . Critics have spent weeks exploring Rockstar's Leonida, featuring the Bonnie-and-Clyde-inspired duo Jason and Lucia, leading to a Metacritic score of 99 . Backed by over 100 reviews, the title is currently listed as the platform's best game of all time , above the original N64 release of The Legend of Zelda: The Ocarina of Time. In the words of The Guardian 's Keza MacDonald: "Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have seen yet." "Leonida is so lifelike that at times it beggars belief, so vast that it feels overwhelming [...] and contains so many potential experiences that it's hard to know where to start." IGN 's Luke Reilly emphasised that the wait for GTA 6 was reflected in the detail Rockstar has poured into its world. "This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I've ever played, and it's one you can interact with at a level never seen before in the series," he said. "Rockstar has truly pushed the boat out.” The game's level of detail raised concerns about performance, particularly its 30fps cap on all consoles , including the PlayStation 5 Pro. However, Reilly found that this limitation did not diminish the experience. "What matters to me is that it looks absolutely incredible and runs smoothly and reliably on a standard PS5. I find all the brilliant visual flourishes far more important, from the concentric rings of ripples on water due to helicopter rotor downwash, to the almost imperceptible line of sweat that appears on Lucia's forehead after a brisk jog, or the buckling of the fabric on a shirt as torsos twist, to the temporary dents on a punching bag as you strike it." "If a sufficiently stable and properly paced 30fps is the route to GTA 6 looking and functioning the way it does, bug-free, then I have no complaints." GTA 6's immersion extends to daily routines that improve stats like health and stamina, or managing car fuel levels. As Game Informer 's Matt Miller observed, these activities "add pacing and counterpoint to the explosive march of major missions, narrative threads, and set-piece encounters that drive the game forward." These everyday moments are initially character-specific, as The New York Times' Yussef Cole noted. "Jason can opt to fix up his run-down bachelor pad in preparation for Lucia's imminent release. There are numerous tasks around the house, like putting up drywall, painting and fixing the roof, that take up the player's time and the character's in-game resources, but they aim toward a productive and satisfying goal: a better relationship." That's not to say GTA 6 isn't like past games, where violence is encouraged and chaos is one petty crime away. Miller emphasised that these moments do not detract from the "meticulously choreographed" set pieces, which "run the gamut from amusing shenanigans at a strip club to intense chases and escapes fueled by raging gunfights and explosions. Many of the best moments leverage an expert sense of musical accompaniment, weaving a slick original score alongside one of the most impressive and wide-ranging licensed soundtracks ever heard in a video game – often to surprisingly emotional effect." Critics agreed that GTA 6 offers unexpected emotional depth, thanks to nuance in both the representation of the lead characters and the player's ability to control them. IGN's Reilly described Jason and Lucia as "unlike any leads that have come before them in the series," whose priorities are each other and escaping the criminal life they find themselves increasingly entrenched in. "They're not angels, and it is invariably their recklessness as small-time crooks that puts them in the wrong place at the wrong time, but the overall sliminess of their far more powerful antagonists does make the couple easy to root for throughout their story,"he wrote. The New York Times' Cole agreed, adding that the emphasis on the duo's relationship "reflects a maturation of a series that has generally only told stories about men solipsistically chasing after their own success." He continued: "Choosing romance is the easy part, thanks to the chemistry and human characterisation of the two leads. Lucia and Jason's relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between." Game Informer's Miller described Jason and Lucia's relationship as "elevating the game to new heights, lending this instalment a heart, tension, and emotional core missing from prior entries." "This is, without a doubt, video gaming's most richly drawn and compelling romance, featuring two leads who are immediately relatable and compelling to watch. Player actions dictate the strength of their bond, deepening the sense of engagement. Like the best crime fiction, you're left surprised by how much you cheer for two people who regularly commit terrible acts." The Guardian's MacDonald "found it impossible not to care" for the couple over time. "They are our avatars in GTA 6's world, but they are not blank stand-ins for the player: you decide their actions but not their personalities. They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim [...] When the story gave me opportunities to decide what would happen next, what came to mind for me was what they would do, not what I would do." sources.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
sources.text: There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. It's fitting I guess that GTA San Andreas is such a strange delight to return to. As I've waited, like everyone else, for GTA 6 , I've been back here in the GTA games of the past, via the slightly dodgy remasters from a few years ago. And what's come through for me, spending a few idle mornings messing around in San Andreas, a game I thought I knew pretty well, is how beautifully odd everything is now. The best part of 20 years have given a game that once strained against its host technology a genuine aesthetic. Surprisingly sparse in detailing, as angular and sheer as dream architecture, in love with expanses, San Andreas is perfectly placed, it seems to me, to capture just how weird California can be. California and Nevada. This is the part I always forget. I mainly think of San Andreas these days through the lens of GTA 5 , which gives you LA and its surroundings but lets the single city serve as the star. It has a bigger footprint than the earlier game, sure, but it uses that space to go deep on the detailing and the sense of a singular, fiercely specific place. San Andreas meanwhile offers three cities - and one of them isn't actually in California. Alongside spins on LA and San Francisco, you get a version of Las Vegas. It's quite neat really: the three points of some arcane spiritual triangle. The kind of thing Marvel Whiteside Parsons, aerospace engineer and Actual Wizard, might have scratched in the dust of his backyard to help him control the weather. He lived - and died - in Pasadena, so all this would have been familiar anyway. There is a classic moment in every GTA. A moment where the map opens up in the early games, or when you explore enough in the later games, and simply get to understand the audacity of what is being attempted here. In San Andreas, and this feels apt, the best way to have this moment is to break the rules, sneaking into the open map before the game is fully ready for you. An early mission allows you to step away from the critical path, as it were, and peg it to the airport in Los Santos, where a plane is waiting to be pinched. Taxi, feel the thrust, and you're off. LA beneath you - sorry, Los Santos - and on the horizon a dinkytown version of the Golden Gate Bridge and the MGM Grand. Dinkytown is the word. From the sky, the huge map of San Andreas, which still feels like an incredible piece of work - such ambition! - can look like toys laid out on a duvet in the remasters. Coming back from GTA 5, a masterpiece of texture, the cities of San Andreas in particular feel very weird - cramped and condensed and wonderfully stagey, arranged the way a kid might jury-rig them together from shoeboxes and stray cardboard. On your way out of Grove Street early on you pass the Los Santos equivalent of the Hollywood sign, looming so close the way it does in the movies but not in the actual city and you feel you could touch it. Downtown is reduced to a handful of the best buildings - it's always pleasing to see the one from the brilliant first act of Speed made the cut - but still manages to capture the important stuff too, which in this case is the way that modern LA looms somewhat cruelly over the old city, captured with a strange sepulchral dignity in the form of the City Hall, so easy to spot but now so small! Elsewhere, the ersatz Las Vega Strip looks like a drawing based on memory - a few of the classic shapes are there, but it's a sketch of a place. In this way, I guess, it captures a truth about Las Vegas. Also, perhaps, it's an admission that this is a town comfortably out of the reach of satire. As for San Francisco, it's a 60s cop movie delight to fishtail around. It nails the hills and what more do you need for a game with cars in it? Taken as a whole these cities feel mesmerising now. And it's the limitations that make them sing, I think: those sheer granite canyons of downtown LA with its towering blocks of architecture and surprisingly thin traffic, with only the very faintest of ambient soundtracks that ensures any gunfire will pop and clap and shake you out of your seat. (Remember, I am playing the remasters and sound effects may be missing.) This is the LA of Repo Man rather than Heat - an otherland where the buildings feel alien, even the air feels alien. At night, palm trees stand out against a sky that glows a deep, clean red. GTA 5 would finesse all of this, the skyboxes and whatnot, but perhaps in that finessing something is lost. (Both games, incidentally, have such a talent for capturing California's kitsch excess that they perhaps miss some of the sweeter truths, such as the astonishing diversity of cultures a city like Los Angeles finds homes for. But how could any game do that justice?) Dinkytowns aside, what San Andreas does better than GTA 5 is space - the peculiar flat spaces of Southern California in particular, a state in which you can never quite tell where the wilderness ends and the landscaping begins, and where the ancient rocks that announce the horizon can look new, like stage settings, while the freeways feel truly ancient, concrete lizards sleeping on the dirt, bleached by the easy sun. sources.title: Miami Heat shows off its 'Vice City hardwood' ahead of the big Grand Theft Auto 6 basketball game
sources.text: They've got new uniforms, too. They're pretty cool. Grand Theft Auto 6 launches at midnight on November 19 in your local time zone , meaning that people in New Zealand will be playing it while I'm still stuck at work on November 18. Unless , that is, you do your gaming on a PC, in which case GTA 6 won't be launching at all—at least, not until some indeterminate span of time has passed and Take-Two Interactive deigns to bestow it upon us. But that doesn't mean we can't indulge in all the pre-release hype, just like everyone else, and so here we are with a look at the "Vice City hardwood," upon which NBA team the Miami Heat—in the guise of the Vice City's hometown team—will square off against the Milwaukee Bucks. It's an extensive overhaul, with a huge Vice City logo at center court, the VI logos in the paint, and the "I Heart Vice City" slogans at either end. Yeah, it's marketing, but I have to admit it looks pretty cool too. Renting an entire NBA team as a promotional tool really puts a finger on just how big Grand Theft Auto 6 is. GTA 5 was big, absolutely, but GTA 6 is huge : Take-Two is looking to make something in the neighborhood of $3.5 billion in GTA 6's launch quarter alone. And it's not just the dollar signs that impress: GTA 6 is also being recognized as a mainstream cultural phenomenon in ways that previous games in the series never were, or could be. It's honestly kind of amazing how far things have come in the past 40+ years. sources.title: Newzoo analyst expects Grand Theft Auto to turn around a rough year for console gaming: 'without GTA 6 the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026'
sources.text: Consoles cost more than ever, and even if you can afford to buy one you don't have as much left over to buy games for it as you used to. That's made 2026 an underwhelming year for console gaming sales, but according to the latest forecast from videogame market analysts Newzoo , the imminent launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will turn that around. "As we explored in the Global Games Market Report 2026," said Newzoo's director of market intelligence, Emmanuel Rosier, "without GTA VI the console market would likely be down year-over-year in 2026. Instead, the game's launch is expected to generate billions of dollars in revenue and give console spending a significant boost." Rosier is the analyst who, back in August, was skeptical about the idea of BioWare surviving long enough to make another Mass Effect game . I wish he'd been wrong about that, but it turned out he was right on the money with that prediction. "Western console has been losing ground," he went on to say. "Its share of global games revenue fell from 21.5% in 2015 to 17.1% in 2025, and its revenue has been broadly flat since 2021. Console adoption shows the same pattern. In Western markets, the console player base has been flat since 2022. Most people who want to play on console already do." Newzoo's prediction is that GTA 6 "will lift console full-game spending by 17.5% this year". But that's just the start of the story. "So while GTA VI is undoubtedly one of the most important releases of the decade," Rosier says, "its initial impact will be concentrated in Western console. That’s still a big market, which we forecast will be worth $36.3 billion in 2026, but it's only part of the industry. The longer-term global story will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online." Though tradition has plenty of people expecting a delay of roughly a year and a half between GTA 6's console and PC releases, general console malaise and the value of GTA Online—likely to be bigger on PC, and perhaps launch alongside the PC port—is a reason to think maybe the wait won't be so long. A recent GamesBeat report claims it'll be out in early 2027. "PC is far bigger than console in several major markets, including China," Rosier says, "and a PC release could expose the game to a much broader international audience. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. "The online mode is another key unknown. Depending on how it's positioned and monetized, it could significantly expand the game's audience. If Rockstar adopts a model that lowers barriers to entry, the long-term opportunity outside the traditional Western console audience could be much larger than it appears today." GTA Online was a huge part of GTA 5 's long-tail success. While Newzoo's data says at least 37% of players who preordered GTA 6 have spent money on GTA Online, only 15% did so in the last 12 months. It's in need of a refresh, and though Rockstar haven't confirmed anything, Twitch's CEO also says GTA 6's multiplayer component will be out in 2027 . sources.title: "We'd love to have you" - New Zealand's tourist board gives a nod to those hopping timezones to play Grand Theft Auto 6 early
sources.text: New Zealand's tourism board has taken advantage of all the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto 6 's launch, as hordes of players who've changed their Xbox timezones to that of the world's second best rugby team (sorry) to jump into the game early. "One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account: PureNewZealand. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you." The post also includes a video of folks looking at all the natural beauty of New Zealand, presumably before they all look themselves indoors to play the video game, alongside the caption: "life, because we're getting GTA 6 first." For those unaware, Xbox owners have been swapping their console time zones for years to New Zealand in order to take advantage of the region's access to games before anywhere else in the world. When games have, let's say, a worldwide release time of midnight across all nations, those living in New Zealand are able to jump in first as a result. Microsoft has for years been happy to let this practice continue on its platform, and as such a sort of cultural norm about hopping on a digital plane for a game's release has been established. If you want guidance, we have a guide on how to pull off the GTA 6 New Zealand trick yourself which can walk you through it. If you aren't keen on doing so for whatever reason, you can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 too . If you want one final run through on what to expect from Rockstar's big release last minute, our Everything We Know about Grand Theft Auto 6 page should set you right for good measure.

sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 review
sources.text: My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third place': the car. I'm slightly skeptical of the obsession with third places these days - love the concept; less convinced that societal bonds are collapsing because today's men aren't spending enough time at their barber's. But here it felt just right: GTA 6 is, of course, a game both about America and about the personal vehicle. The clue's in the name. And as you play GTA 6, you realise, over and over, that the car is where so much of this game happens. It's where you take calls that lead to missions or story developments; where you pick up, hang out with, and chat to your partner; where you race away from police, gangs, wild animals and weirdos. Where you do much of your discovery of this properly, disorientatingly, astoundingly big and detailed world. Where you'll be when you find the most 'emergent events'. And, more than it's ever been before, the car is now an essential partner in itself; a place to stow weapons, disguises, and stolen goods - a companion it feels almost impossible to do without. I could go on about this. GTA 6 is a game of perpetual motion, as protagonists Jason and Lucia do their best to outrun a world that so often feels a step ahead - and which often culminates in some of the most exhilarating, astonishing chase sequences ever built in a video game. GTA 5 , its Los Santos-set predecessor, was aware enough of the importance of the car to name an in-game canyon after Reyner Banham, the British architectural critic who described Los Angeles' freeway system, one of the city's "four ecologies", as "Autopia". So yes: the car is the third place, in modern America and in GTA 6. The place of self-actualisation between work and home - two points that, for GTA 6's protagonists in particular, seem to always be in a state of flux. Maybe the car's their true home. For the longest time I really thought that idea summed up GTA 6 quite nicely. Until I didn't. Reducing GTA 6 to just the car, I realised, looking at it through only that one lens, forces you to be too narrow. You miss too much of it. What about the romance? The sensuality? The people and the natural world? And so what I've come to settle on instead - and honestly I expect this to change many more times over the coming days and weeks too, as even more of this horizonless game rolls back to reveal itself - is that GTA 6 just doesn't have a single thread to pull on. No one thing that, when properly grasped, suddenly draws it into a manageable shape. I've no doubt we'll all try. People have, for whatever reason, always reached for the most reductive ideas when they talk about Grand Theft Auto in particular. Maybe it's a natural response to something too big and unwieldy to instantly get your head around: to seize the first acceptable idea and declare it just 'x' . To admit something is too complex for you to immediately summarise is far less comfortable than simply dismissing it on the spot. Whatever it is, GTA 6 isn't just anything. For one, every thing it is also seems to have an opposite. It's vast - incomprehensibly vast - but also overloaded with miniscule detail. It's about big ideas, themes, places - America, society, love - and also about individuals. It's ridiculous and puerile, and also sometimes mature. Tender and violent. Deep and shallow. Novel and, in places, surprisingly familiar. It's both a big adventure playground of video game activities and a focused story of suffocating intensity. Whatever foible might arise, the game presents you with a ready-made answer - often quite literally: you can turn off notifications about your relationship status in the menu if you just want to ignore that part. You can switch to the old controls (GTA 6 has seen a bit of a control overhaul), from the first screen you're shown. Or simply tear off in the opposite direction to whatever it is that dissatisfies you and do something else. If there's an idea to reduce this game to, then, the best I can manage is this: maybe Grand Theft Auto 6 is a game designed to be irreducible. None of that is to say it's perfect. It's easy to stand in front of something like this and just bask in the awe of it, forgetting to stop a moment and step back. The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome, but there are also nits to pick. But then you step back again and they tend to fade away. GTA 6 will not be for everyone. But no game has made a better attempt at being everything. GTA 6's story begins with Jason and Lucia. Discussing it beyond that is, frankly, almost impossible to do with any kind of substance without also spoiling it. For all the precipitous leaks, Rockstar has kept its story's two most essential moments - its beginning and its end - entirely secret, and without those two moments we're only really left with euphemisms. Jason and Lucia are on the run, after a seemingly simple fetch quest goes awry. Who they're running from, or why they're being chased quite so hard, remains agonisingly beyond their field of view. But what is clear, right from the off, is exactly why they're so determined to escape. And amongst all this Rockstar has achieved something kind of momentous, when it comes to Grand Theft Auto: we've got real and very human stakes. What else can be said? Well, let's go back to Rockstar's decision to begin so explicitly with Jason and Lucia. This is a story about a relationship. You can nurture or neglect it, but fundamentally that relationship - however strong - is at the heart of things. sources.text: Thirteen years later, Rockstar has crafted a worthy successor to GTA V and the new standard-bearer for open-world games. How do you follow a game like Grand Theft Auto V ? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behind Tetris and Minecraft on the list of the best-selling games of all time, and its lucrative online mode has helped it remain popular for well over a decade. That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the next GTA . A series of major leaks and delays only exacerbated this. At a time when much of the video game industry is struggling , the next edition of GTA stands alone , a cultural moment so big ( almost ) everybody has been forced to get out of the way . The buildup to Grand Theft Auto VI ’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen. Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait. At this point I’ve spent nearly 80 hours in Leonida, GTA VI ’s fictional take on Florida. And what I’ve experienced is a game that combines the wide-open freedom offered in GTA V with the remarkable level of immersion from the studio’s 2018 release Red Dead Redemption 2 , while also improving on both qualities. At the same time, it’s also the most mature GTA game Rockstar has ever made, merging the criminal antics and absurdist humor the series is known for with a love story that gives you new ways to interact with the world and new reasons for wanting to push forward. This is the GTA game the studio has been building toward for its entire existence. Let’s start with that new premise. GTA V introduced the idea of multiple protagonists to the series, and VI takes that concept in a different direction. It’s a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired story about Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals who meet while, of course, stealing a car. It’s the most GTA -possible meet-cute. The idea is that you can play as both characters individually and also build their relationship over the course of the game. Things start out relatively slow. At the outset, Lucia is in prison, and you play solely as Jason, getting things ready for when she gets out. You can fix up your ramshackle house — that involves actually nailing down new stairs and rolling out paint on the walls — and also start building up a nest egg through means that are not exactly legal. Jason and Lucia’s relationship grows naturally over the course of the game, but it’s also a slow buildup to becoming the inseparable pair they were by the end of my playthrough. GTA VI approaches most of the experience with confident and deliberate pacing. Even when you control them individually, the characters are often together, either just hanging out or partnering for a crime. And being able to play as both is one of the game’s standout features. But I didn’t get to that point in the game until almost 17 hours in. Before that, you play as both leads mostly solo, learning who they are as people, before you’re given free rein to switch between the two. What’s great about the premise is how seamlessly it fits with what you’re actually doing in the game. There’s some bigger-picture stuff that I won’t spoil, but generally speaking, the main goal in GTA VI is to make a lot of money so that Jason and Lucia can get out of the criminal life for good and retire somewhere comfortably. And outside of the big story missions, you’re largely free to choose how you go about that. You can rob jewelry stores, steal cars, raid drug dens, or even search for hidden treasure at the bottom of the sea. Over the course of the game you’ll also meet different criminals who serve as fences, so you can sell them whatever you’ve got to build up your savings account. Sometimes they’ll even text you targets that are particularly lucrative. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. I’m not a big fan of armed robbery, for instance. There are just so many things that can go wrong, and I almost always end up killing some innocent bystander when I try to escape. But I love getaway chases, and so stealing cars became my main form of income. Most importantly, though, this structure gives you a lot of reasons to go out in the world and explore. The missions take you all over the map — which is actually entirely accessible from the very beginning, if you choose to play that way — including not only the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City, but also tourist beaches, swamps, trailer parks, and a wild variety of other locations, each with its own landscape to explore and characters to meet. To be clear: Despite being larger, more mature, and more lifelike, this is still very much GTA . This is a game about chaos and crime. This comes across in a few ways. First, there are those smaller missions where you never really know how things will play out. The cashier at the pawn shop you’re robbing might have a shotgun, or you might accidentally smash into a big rig during a high-speed getaway. The world itself is full of unpredictable moments that force you to think on your feet. Several times I stopped my car to talk to an NPC whose vehicle broke down on the side of the road. In one instance the driver just swore at me to leave her alone. In another, I got pulled into an entire storyline involving a delivery driver who needed help to keep her AI chatbot manager off her back. I delivered her packages and ended up dealing with everything from porch pirates to tigers. The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. sources.text: Well, whaddaya know? Turns out all you need to make a great videogame is around a decade of time, the GDP of a BRICS nation, and a marketing machine pervasive to the point of totalitarianism. The reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6 —Rockstar's sequel to that game that would splash " GOURANGA !" on the screen when you ran over enough people—are in. People like it a lot. No, really, they're out of their gourd for this one, folks. GTA 6 might just be the most absurdly hyped game in history, and yet the mad lads at Rockstar really seem to have pulled it off. Of course, the game's true test—its review on PC Gamer dot com and its accompanying magazine—hasn't happened yet. We'll have to wait for the all-but-certain PC port for that. For now, you can read our impressions of the console version here . But our console brethren have been putting pen to paper to get their thoughts down, and the reviews for GTA 6 are flowing thick and fast. Here's a sample platter of them, to give you an idea of just how nuts people are going for this thing. GameSpot's Tamoor Hussain paints a picture of Leonida that overflows with detail, calling it "a game of staggering scope and scale obsessed with small details that could be lost in its vastness, a giant haystack full of needles that you’ll constantly find, creating delight in their improbable discovery". I get the impression that a year from now, five years, ten years, there will still be people rushing to subreddits and forums (if we still have those) to ask if others have seen this or that little detail Rockstar tucked into some obscure corner of its humungous world. A second perfect score from the gang at IGN, whose Luke Reilly had a great time doing things like: Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. Most of which you could feasibly cram into a game whose goal was to simulate my dad, but in GTA 6 it all forms part of a world that constantly surprises you with things to do. "I see no real limit to the amount of time I could spend here, endlessly exploring and interacting with Vice City and the massive area surrounding it", writes Reilly, adding that—despite having beaten the game with 120 hours of playtime under his belt—"While the well-paced story effectively nudged me around the map, there are still vast sections of it that I’m yet to even visit". Our brothers in arms at GR note that GTA 6 is an improvement on every entry in the series before it: "there's no aspect of the series' gameplay that hasn't been improved over past instalments", writes Josh West, who calls the game (affectionately) "the ultimate time vampire" where "every one of your actions ultimately impacts the lives of Jason and Lucia". Honestly, sounds like a nerve-wracking amount of responsibility for me. The New York Times – Too stately to give a review score but it's an "NYT Critic’s Pick" You know a videogame has broken containment when the grey lady is getting in on the review beat. The NYT's Yussef Cole zeroed in on GTA 6's heart in his review: the relationship between protagonists Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos—"This is a game about love and relationships, their joy and heartache, and the work required to make them successful", he writes, noting that players can choose to hold hands with their paramour at the touch of a button. We've come a little ways from beating people to death with dildos, folks (though you may well still be able to do that; I'd be surprised if you couldn't). Giant Bomb (shoutout to Charlie Tunoku) joins in with the hosannahs for GTA 6, describing it as one of those games that feels like a step up for the medium as a whole. "Grand Theft Auto VI is Rockstar’s best game", writes Dan Ryckert. "In the thirteen years between entries of one of the biggest franchises in entertainment, fans’ expectations grew to a level that felt unrealistic. Somehow, Rockstar has managed to overdeliver on the most hyped video game of all time". The Guardian's Keza MacDonald writes that Rockstar's Leonida is so realistic as to defy belief, but that in its humid, gator-ridden byways you will find scope for both "foulmouthed, OTT chaos—as well as new empathy for the fugitive couple at its centre". It is a game, it seems, that is almost too big and varied to squeeze into something like a regular review. "it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start". But you bet those experiences are many, varied, and shockingly fleshed-out. He opens with a description of one of the random events that can happen to players in the game, in which he witnessed a crash and found himself enlisted into an NPC's scam to sue a parody of Amazon for millions. "Incidents like this, elaborate depictions of a heightened reality, happen constantly in Grand Theft Auto 6", he writes. "The joy of Grand Theft Auto VI, much like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Elden Ring before it, comes from discovering its world’s delights and seeing how it reacts to your actions". It perhaps tells us something that the only non-perfect score on this list is… a 4.5/5 overflowing with praise. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 GTA 6 Rockstar Games Tips Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here. The long wait was totally worth it. It is one of the best games I’ve played in many years and easily the best Grand Theft Auto game ever made. It is also a big, complicated, and deep game, with so much to do and see. So, to help you out, here’s a bunch of tips for players hopping into GTA 6 this week. Don’t worry, no spoilers are included below. Without spoiling anything, there are some incredibly big surprises and really memorable moments buried in this game. I highly recommend that people avoid watching too many videos about GTA 6 ahead of playing it to avoid ruining one particular late-game moment that might be one of my favorite video game surprises in years. Before you rush out the door to do some missions or rob a liquor store, take a moment to grab a bite and a drink. These items will buff your health, stamina, and focus meter, letting you take more damage, run longer, and slow down time more during combat. And hey, don’t assume that just because you’re drinking a soda or eating a hot dog, you have to stop moving or shooting. In GTA 6 , you can move, shoot, run, hold hands, and even drive while holding and eating food. Finally, you can crack a cold one while shooting a rifle. Around the map, you’ll encounter dogs and cats. If you hold the left trigger, you can zoom in on them and then praise and pet them. And you should do this, not just because dogs and cats are great, but also because it buffs your focus and rewards you with some good behavior points toward your criminal profile. In GTA 6 , you can store guns and clothes in your personal car’s trunk. And you should do this, as changing clothes is a great and fast way to lose the attention of the police. You can manage your clothing, create new custom outfits, and store clothes in your trunk at any clothing store with a changing room, so don’t feel like you have to head back home to change your outfits around or remove stuff from your trunk. Just find a store. Also, Rockstar lets you rename your custom outfits using a list of pre-existing words, like clubbing, hunting, or everyday. I recommend doing that to make it easier at a glance to see what everything stored in your trunk actually is without having to put it on and check. When you go out shopping for clothesâand you will likely do that because dressing up is so much fun in this gameâbring both Jason and Lucia. This will let you buy clothing for both of them, try on new items as either character, and modify their current attire. And bonus: Buying clothing for your partner gets you some extra romance points. The world of Leonida is packed with random events and moments that you can encounter while just walking around. These can be as simple as a drug deal going bad, or as complex as someone who needs help finding their missing spouse after a night partying. Often these events will be signaled to the player via shouting or other loud noises. If you hear something like that, click the left and right sticks to activate focus mode and find the source of the commotion, and then go investigate it. I spent many hours making sure to close it first, then realized it closed when you drive away. You can also hold left on the D-pad to access your car’s features, including the ability to turn off headlights and close (or open) the trunk. Plus, it’s just fun to explore the ocean. On Jason and Lucia’s phones, you’ll find an app called Scooter Bros. This lets you manage your owned vehicles, spawn them near you, and even repair them. However, this isn’t free and early on money will be tight, so be careful how often you rely on this convenient app. It can also get vehicles out of police impound lots, but that ain’t cheap. It costs $12,500 to upgrade to the premium version of the Scooter Bros service, which, for many hours in the game, is going to be more than you can spare. But once you feel comfortable spending that much, I recommend it. It gives you three free uses of the app every in-game day, which saves money in the long run. Plus, the app is upgraded and says you’re premium, and that’s nice. Eventually, GTA 6 will let you buy garages around the map. These aren’t very useful while driving about, but they do give you more slots to store cars and motorcycles as you build up Jason and Lucia’s fleet of personal vehicles. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Performance Is Mostly Stable, Except On Xbox Series S Where It Can Hit Sub-20FPS
sources.text: With Grand Theft Auto 6 âs world being as big as it is and current consoles being six years old, thereâs naturally a bit of worry about how the game performs on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Our reviewer played the game on a PS5 Pro, considered to be the most powerful console on the market right now, and said that while it runs at 30 frames-per-second most of the time, there were still some noticeable frame drops in crowded areas. But if you havenât bought a PS5 Pro, what can you expect from GTA 6 âs performance? Well, the folks over at Digital Foundry have done what they do best and created some lengthy technical breakdowns of the game, including stress testing it in explosive situations. According to their video, the PS5 Pro tends to hold a pretty solid 30fps, unless you go around making a mess by blowing up a lot of cars at once; in those moments Digital Foundry saw the game dip to around 24fps at its lowest. The base PS5, however, seems to struggle to maintain 30fps in the best of cases, and if you decide to cause a lot of on-screen destruction, those dips are actually sustained until you leave an area.Â On the Xbox side, the Xbox Series X seems to share the same relative stability as the PS5 Pro, with the same frame drops during car chases, crowded scenes, or firefights when things get busier on screen. The big question is how the Xbox Series S, which was originally released in 2020 as a cheaper, lower-powered alternative to the bougie, more expensive consoles of the year, handles GTA 6 . According to Digital Foundry , there are some details that are less prevalent or rendered with lower-res textures, and the resolution is lower, coming in at 720p compared to the 1440p of Series X. The DF video has a number of comparison shots demonstrating how a lot of small details have been downgraded on Series S, but the real difference is that the framerate is, unsurprisingly, struggling the most on the less powerful Xbox. Digital Foundry reports that while 30fps is the target, even the most “typical” play can affect framerate, with standard combat encounters and car chases dropping it to around 25 and the more demanding carnage bringing it down to 20. There’s even a few seconds in the video where it gets down to 18 and 19fps during an explosive shootout. Ultimately, if youâre hoping for the smoothest possible experience, the PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X are the unsurprising winners here. A PC version of the game is rumored to launch sometime next year , and I imagine thatâs where folks with high-end builds are going to be able to get smoother, 60fps framerates as Rockstar apparently has no plans to add a Performance Mode to GTA6 on consoles. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the smoothest GTA game in history" despite 30fps, analysis finds
sources.text: GTA 6's frame rate isn't flawless, but it's substantially better than how its predecessors launched GTA 6 is finally here – well, depending on your time zone, anyway. In any case, it's a real video game that people are actually playing, which means it's time to discuss the game's most important aspect: its resolution and frame rate. According to a new tech analysis, Rockstar has managed to coax solid performance out of the current-gen consoles even while pursuing nigh-unprecedented levels of fidelity. "GTA 6 is a 30 frames per second game, but that also kind of makes it the smoothest GTA game in history, at least at launch," as tech analyst John Linneman explains in a new Digital Foundry video . "Every previous entry ran significantly worse on the original target hardware. Whether that trade-off is worthwhile, however, is entirely up to the individual. But as things stand, I'm not convinced that they could have achieved 60 frames per second in a game of this scope on this class of hardware." It's now trivial to play previous GTA games at 60fps or above, but each previous 3D entry targeted 30fps on its original platforms and regularly dipped below that target. GTA 6's hold on its 30fps target is much stronger. On base PS5 and Xbox Series X (which Digital Foundry covered in a separate analysis ), the game will dip below 30fps at times when, say, screaming down the road at speed, but those dips are "very minor." If you really try to break the game by heading into a busy intersection with a grenade launcher and causing chaos, you can cause the frame rate to take a more sustained dive, but you'll get a solid experience in the course of normal play. While you can get some dips with the kind of chaos on PS5 Pro, the whole experience seems to be even smoother on Sony 's high-end hardware. "I spent most of my time on the PS5 Pro, which is the best way to play this game by far," Linneman says. "You basically get a near-flawless 30fps update. The frame pacing is perfect, cutscenes consistent and fluid, unlike older Rockstar titles, and everything moves without hiccups or stutters." Yes, that does also mean Rockstar's finally fixed the cutscene judder that's plagued its games since GTA 4 . The miracles continue. Well, there is one exception, as you probably shouldn't expect any miracles on Xbox Series S. Microsoft 's lower-end machine retains most of the graphical features of its more fully-featured counterparts, which I suppose is miraculous in its own way, but its frame rate brings us back to the peak of Xbox 360 gaming, with sustained drops into the 20fps range whenever there's real action on-screen. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more While Rockstar's decision to go 30fps with GTA 6 has been controversial , Linneman is "more willing to forgive it due to just how far it's pushing the visuals." He adds, "it feels like tasting the future." Check out our full GTA 6 review if you're interested in, you know, the actual game rather than the frame rates. 4. sources.title: How to Take Drugs in Grand Theft Auto 6? Where to Find Drugs, Explained
sources.text: We’ve known for quite a while that we’ll be able to consume drugs in Grand Theft Auto 6. It was one of the elements we learned about that firmly established it as one of the most mature GTA games ever made. It mirrors Red Dead in terms of live consumption, but from what we know, you can consume things like cocaine at the press of a button. But how exactly do you do that? How do you take drugs in GTA 6? And how do you get more drugs when you’ve run out? In this guide, we’ll explain how it all works and answer those questions. If you want to find your fix in GTA 6, you’ll be happy to know it’s not so hard to get your hands on some drugs. Like many other things, you’ll find narcotics on downed enemies. For instance, you might eliminate someone to find a baggie of cocaine in their pocket. This is a relatively simple way to find drugs in GTA 6. Alternatively, you might stumble upon some pills or powder when digging through a mission location, just like you might find healing items, ammunition, or food. That’s not all, though. This game is bursting with dynamic events, and one that we’ve seen saw a plane crash nearby while we were exploring. On board was a stash of cocaine packages, and we racked up around $10,000 after taking and selling the stash to Brian, your ‘boss’, whom you meet very early in the game. These events are very random and unpredictable, just to keep the world as emergent as possible, so you might see something immediately, or you might never see it. That’s the beauty of this game. If we’re talking about less hard substances, you can buy cigarettes and alcohol at liquor, convenience, and grocery stores. To consume drugs and break that straight-edge lifestyle in GTA 6, you’ll need to do what you might have done in Red Dead Redemption 2, holding LB/L1 to open your loadout, switching to the items tab, and locating the drugs and smokes field in the upper left of the wheel. From there, you can scroll through what’s available. You might have cigarettes, cigars, bags of cocaine, or something else entirely. Once you’re satisfied with your pick, select the item to consume it. You’ll get buffs and debuffs from whatever you consume. For instance, cocaine overcharges your stamina and aggression factor, but it negates your overall health bar, so you mix the good with the bad. sources.text: Includes the return of Now & Later Packs, MLB The Show 26 community stats, and more. Before we dive into new information on MLB The Show 27, let’s take a look back. As we reflect on 2026, two things stand out above everything else: the incredible passion and support of the MLB The Show community, and our need to better communicate and react to community feedback going forward. Whether you’ve been playing for decades or joined us for the first time this year, you’ve helped make this another special chapter in our franchise’s history. While we’re proud of what our team accomplished this year, we recognize that the heart of MLB The Show has always been its community. Since launch, you’ve hit an astonishing: You’ve also drawn 123,300,616 walks and racked up a staggering 2,130,551,161 strikeouts. It seems we have some work to do on our collective plate discipline and pitch recognition! But it’s not all strikeouts. You’ve also recorded 18,666,758 Perfect-Perfect hits and scored an incredible 2,506,757,548 runs. And if those numbers weren’t impressive enough, the community collectively spent the equivalent of 31,541 years playing MLB The Show this year. This year was not without some issues and hopefully over the next few months we’ll show you how we’ve made improvements in a host of areas.Your stories, feedback, creativity, and passion remind us why we do what we do. We don’t take your time, trust, or support for granted, and we’re incredibly fortunate to have a community that cares so deeply about the game. From all of us at San Diego Studio, thank you for another unforgettable year. We’re excited about what lies ahead and look forward to continuing this journey together. So, what lies ahead? We’re eager to share the exciting new features and improvements coming to MLB The Show 27, but it’s still a little too early to reveal what’s in store. However, there’s one announcement we can’t wait to make: The Tech Test is officially returning for MLB The Show 27. Tech Tests are invaluable to the development process. They help our team identify bugs, evaluate performance, and gather meaningful feedback from the community before the game officially launches. Now, you might be wondering: If Tech Tests are so important, why haven’t we held one since MLB The Show 23? That’s a fair question. Game development is challenging, and each year brings its own set of difficult decisions and competing priorities. Some of those decisions resulted in us not holding Tech Tests for the past few years. We appreciate your patience, passion, and continued support, and we’re looking forward to having you be part of the process again. We will provide more details on the Tech Test in the new year. There is still more ahead for MLB The Show 26 , and the time you spend playing can give you a head start in MLB The Show 27. Now & Later packs are coming back. Now & Later Packs contain items you can use now in MLB The Show 26, with the added bonus of allowing you to redeem The Show Packs “later” in MLB The Show 27 at no additional cost. Each Now & Later Pack you earn playing Diamond Dynasty Content in MLB The Show 26 on console will give out a Now & Later voucher that will automatically be redeemed into The Show Packs when logging into MLB The Show 27 on console during its standard release. Make sure you log into ‘27 with the same account you used to earn Now & Later Packs in ‘26. While that’s all for today, in the meantime, get a head start and start earning those Now & Later Packs in MLB The Show 26. We look forward to sharing more soon and are excited about what’s to come in 2027. In the meantime, for the latest MLB The Show news, head to TheShow.com , sign up for The Scouting Report , and follow our official social channels.

sources.text: November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before. 2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred , Control Resonant , Mixtape , Pragmata , The Blood of Dawnwalker , Star Wars: Galactic Racer , 007 First Light , Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve … seriously, all these games came out this year . That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19. You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too. XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time . Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one , so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach. You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it. If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do. We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair. Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in. We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify . XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking . Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions. Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

sources.title: Caves of Qud's first DLC is forcing its devs to ask important questions: 'How does a crab get high?'
sources.text: Qud's co-creators discuss dogs with guns, handless tattooing, and the tragedy of a sinning tree. In a GDC interview with Freehold Games in 2025, I asked the developers of magnificently mutated, indulgently arcane science-fantasy roguelike Caves of Qud the same thing anyone would in my situation: What's the ideal number of limbs for a being to aspire to? Their answer was none, because "a perfect sphere is the ideal form" and "we started in perfection and only moved farther from God." As you can imagine, I was eager to speak with co-creators Brian Bucklew and Jason Grinblat earlier this month about Diaspora, the roguelike's upcoming first expansion . Diaspora aims to add an "influx of riotous life" to Qud, expanding its body plan-agnostic mutation system with playable animal and plant characters. With Qud's mutagenic possibility space about to erupt even further, I posed its developers another pressing question: Is it a greater moral tragedy for a sin to be committed by a man who mutated into a tree, or by a tree who mutated into a man? "We have text on this in-game," Grinblat said, citing Aphorisms About Birds —an in-game book which notes that our fairy tales pay plenty of attention to the man who's turned into a bird, but little to the cruelty fate's inflicted on the bird who's turned into a man. "I think that's probably even more true if you're a tree. There's one tree mayor in the game. He's pretty happy. He's been around for a while. If he were a guy just walking around out there, getting acid gas shot at him, I think he'd be pretty upset." "It hits too close to home, right? We're having trouble in our world dealing with things transforming into the facsimile of man," Bucklew said. "It's hard for me to think about turning into the facsimile of man without becoming sad about the way the world is and how real that question's going to be in our lives for the next 20 years." Conversely, Grinblat noted, "becoming a tree sounds really nice." To that, Bucklew agreed, wondering whether "there's some way we can get into that business," possibly through marketing "some random peptide." With an air of existential horror comfortably established, we moved into a more mechanical discussion of Diaspora's new plant and animal playstyles. In Caves of Qud, it's already possible for a player character to end up with all sorts of bodies: A mutant character could end up sprouting a bouquet of new limbs and body parts, each capable of equipping items and using abilities. And a number of the game's existing mutations allow a character to acquire some very animalian or plantlike characteristics, whether it's antlers, ape fur, or photosynthetic skin. With Diaspora's plant and animal gene-stocks, however, the developers are aiming to lean even harder into exploring what more specialized body types provide—and what they don't. "I'm a crab: I have six legs, I might have a claw. I'm a bear: I'm a quadruped that doesn't have hands in a traditional sense. That's already a space to play with." That's elaborated on further with species traits, a new feature exclusive to Diaspora character types. Species traits are a kind of stock-specific mutation bonus, representing the inherent features of an animal's—or plant's—anatomy. While a human character can mutate wings, a mutant bird's inherent wing mutation will advance faster and allow access to new, bird-specific flight advancements. Same with tails: Mutant animal characters that possess a tail as a species trait will be able to mutate the appendage to be prehensile more quickly than mutant characters that don't. "We want every animal to have something weird and unique about them that you can't just get if you were a human and you advance that mutation a bunch," Grinblat said. Species traits will introduce a breadth of new opportunities for Qud's already-rich buildcrafting, but creating a new plant or animal character will mean opting out of some things that are standard to the human experience. For example: If I make a mutant dog, can I hold a gun without mutating new hands or opposable thumbs? "This is a big thing. No," Grinblat said. "Right now, no." There are, of course, ways for my mutant dog to achieve its dreams of weapon-wielding. I might seek out the helping hands artifact already present in-game, which provides the wearer with two extra arms and hands—or I could pick up that aforementioned prehensile tail mutation and grant my tail the gift of gunslinging. But while Grinblat acknowledged that "hands are very powerful," he said implementing those kinds of natural animal limitations are an intentional design decision, made in the hopes that players will explore new ways of surviving Qud's countless dangers. "You might end up with a dog with a gun, but you might be doing a lot of dog stuff—running with a pack of dogs who each do their own thing," Grinblat said. "What an actual dog looks like in Qud is up for grabs, but we want to encourage different playstyles that animals can lean into without just feeling like, 'oh, I'm always going to get hands and use guns.'" Unfortunately for Freehold, introducing a yet wider gradient of body types into the absurd complexity of Qud's systems and simulations has produced exciting new problems to solve—and philosophical riddles to ponder. "We've spent so much time figuring out the ontology of tails," Bucklew said. "Are tails arms? Can they wear bracelets? How different is a prehensile tail from a regular tail? Is a tail different from a head in terms of what it can wear? A necklace? A bracelet? A lot of hours in meetings about tail ontology." sources.title: As blockbuster game releases run scared from GTA 6, meet the brave devs tackling Rockstar's behemoth head-on
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 . It's got cool cars, crime, a big new city to explore, and the potential to hoover up so much player time that many developers have chosen to give it the widest berth possible. It's led to an October uncommonly packed with big-hitters, and a November - ordinarily one of gaming's biggest months - that's near-barren. But not every developer is steering clear. Despite the potential risks, a select few have looked at GTA 6 and seen not a threat but an opportunity, so what's driving these brave souls? Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School, a first-person puzzle adventure with a popular predecessor, was originally set to launch this September, but like many games this year saw its release date moved. However, its developer bucked the industry trend, shifting its sequel not away from GTA 6's orbit, but closer. "The thing that scares me more than this monocultural event - GTA 6 - is releasing in a week when there are like 15 good games rather than one big one", Coin Crew Games co-founder Wyatt Bushnell tells me when I ask about the studio's decision. Escape Academy 2's original release date might have kept it away from Grand Theft Auto 6, but it would have instead faced a potential "bloodbath" of competition from the likes of Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Blood of the Dawnwalker, Control Resonant, and more. "That was our rationale," Bushnell says. "We can still cut into the GTA stuff, but it would have been a lot harder in September and October." It helps, notes Bushnell, that Escape Academy 2 and Grand Theft Auto 6 - one a contemplative puzzle game, the other a blockbuster action spectacle - are serving very different crowds. That's a sentiment echoed by David Lowey, Atari's senior director of sales and marketing. Atari has similarly bucked industry trends and is releasing two games - Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered and Barbie Rewind - in the now largely vacant November window. When we speak, Lowey says there's a clear logic to smaller companies "sneaking" into spots that bigger-budget games can't risk filling, especially if their games differ greatly from Grand Theft Auto 6. "Look at Barbie Rewind coming out on the 12th," he elaborates. "It's a retro game, so it'll pull in people who grew up with these games [and] there's the cosy dreamhouse design at the core ... which is a vastly different game type to GTA 6 and plenty of other games. "It's not an FPS, not a high-octane action game, there's not a lot of combat," Lowey continues. "It's designed to be the exact opposite. It's a game you're meant to curl up in a chair and play." And while he acknowledges the "reality of modern gaming" means there'll be some audience overlap between Barbie Rewind and GTA 6 players - "These sort of older ideas of what people play by gender and age have been smashed", he says - it "won't be the biggest overlap in the world". That, then, makes going toe-to-toe an easier bet. But for Bushnell and Escape Academy, there's another consideration making GTA 6's launch window feel less of a risk: longer-tail sales. "The traditional thinking is that you have this big release and make all of your money in those first two weeks," he explains. "I don't think that holds a tonne of water anymore. The vast majority of sales for Escape Academy were made well after its release. The reality is with digital distribution, discounting, and the fact there is this shelf of games, we're in a world where games last far longer than their initial launch." That means it's less of a concern if GTA 6 sucks up everyone's attention for a few weeks. sources.title: GTA 6's Completely Unrealistic Mountains Had to Be in the Game, Rockstar Says
sources.text: GTA 6 takes some liberties with its world around Vice City If you’ve ever spent time in and around Miami, Grand Theft Auto 6 is bound to delight you. Rockstar Games spared no expense in bringing the diverse world of Florida to life in digital form. Walk down the street in Vice City, and you’re sure to find an approximation of a bar you’ve actually been to . Head to the Leonida Keys, and you’ll find rows of houses on stilts. The attention to detail is impressive, but it also makes one odd detail about the map a little odd. Go all the way north in Leonida, right up to Lummox County, and you’ll be able to go hiking and hunting in the mountains. As any Floridian will tell you, that’s not exactly reflective of the real Florida’s topography. Why take such a major creative liberty there when so much else about Leonida is grounded in realism? In an interview with Polygon, Rockstar North co-head Rob Nelson explained why GTA 6 takes players to the mountains. Nelson said that one of the biggest challenges the team faced when designing the game was figuring out the map. Rockstar’s map team began working on the game in 2015, Nelson said, well before anyone else at the studio. While creating another city was easy enough for a team that has mastered that art, expanding to surrounding Florida locales was a tougher proposition. That’s because Florida is a very flat state. The problem with depicting it as is, though, is that GTA players likely would have some expectations about what should be in a modern GTA map. GTA 5 , for instance, built off of Los Angeles to create Los Santos. Because of that, the map has a lot of variety in elevation. That wouldn’t be possible if Leonida stuck too close to reality, so Rockstar ultimately decided to include some mountains to keep GTA 6 a little more consistent with GTA 5 . Though it may not be accurate, it’s a welcome addition to the map. As fun as it is to drive around Vice City, weaving around the same highways can get old. Lummox County offers a lot more open space for off-roading, biking, and other activities that just wouldn’t be possible in a city. For instance, when I found a bicycle perched atop a hill, I found myself racing down a natural BMX course that was built into the world. Every time I head up to Lummox County, it feels like I’m on vacation. Crucially, it’s also the best date spot in the entire game. You can take Jason and Lucia out on impromptu dates throughout GTA 6 , letting the couple play some mini-golf together or blow off steam at a shooting range. One of my favorite play sessions so far simply happened when I got the two in a truck and took them up north to a part of the map I’d never seen. We got out when we found a hiking trail and wound up stumbling into some ruins high up on a hill. It was a peaceful moment of discovery that the two got to share together. Moments like that are what make GTA 6 special, and Leonida’s intricate design is the thing that powers it all.

Jason’s friend Cal mentions that if Lucia’s going to live at Jason’s house, he better fix the place up. Stand next to them and you’ll be able to repair the steps and enter Jason’s house. To fix the leaky roof in GTA 6, head outside Jason’s house and find the set of ladders that are stacked next to the door. This is a quick way to make sure that Jason and Lucia get off on a strong foot, and it takes very little time to do. That’s our complete guide to fixing Jason’s house in GTA 6.

sources.text: Publisher Kniv Studio and developer Dreamery have announced Attention Addicted NEET , a multi-ending visual novel where players experience the changes in a girl who shuts herself away at home because she doesn’t want to get a job. It will be available for PC via Steam . A release date was not announced. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : Attention Addicted NEET is a visual novel with a multi-ending story, where you experience the changes in a girl who shuts herself away at home because she doesn’t want to get a job. When her influencer little sister cuts off her allowance, telling her to ‘go out and get a job,’ she reluctantly turns to social media. She thought social media influencers made money easily. Since then, she has been carried along by attention unlike anything she has ever experienced, gradually becoming addicted to it. The attention she gets from the fools in internet communities makes her sad, excited, and sometimes angry. The job her little sister hoped she’d get grows more distant, while her follower count keeps rising. Will our protagonist, Miyu, give up all this social media influencer business and find a stable job, as her little sister wishes?
